{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=reward+misspecification+detection+reinforcement+learning+invariant+properties&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.31234/osf.io/bjyr9\", \"title\": [\"Achieving Scale-Invariant Reinforcement Learning Performance with Reward Range Normalization\"], \"abstract\": \"

The performance of standard reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms depends on the scale of the rewards they aim to maximize. Various strategies have been proposed to tackle this issue, but these usually restrict the algorithms' ability to adapt to varying task conditions and evolve in open-ended environments. Inspired by human cognitive processes, we propose leveraging a well-known cognitive bias to develop scale-invariant RL algorithms: reward range normalization. We compare a classical RL algorithm to one leveraging reward range-adaptation, finding that while the standard model’s accuracy is limited to certain reward magnitudes, the range-adapted model maintains consistent performance across all magnitudes. We next show that range-adaptation acts as autonomously adjusting the exploration rate, keeping it close to optimal for any given reward scale. Further, we show that the range-adapted model extends effectively to more complex, noisy, dynamic, and multi-step tasks.

\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/bjyr9_v2\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 9, 5]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/springerreference_178761\", \"title\": [\"Average-Reward Reinforcement Learning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/springerreference_178761\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6946592\", \"title\": [\"GRPO-MMS: Reinforcement Learning with a Composite Reward for Multimodal Fraud Message Detection\"], \"abstract\": \"As text-only interception matures, fraudsters increasingly hide deceptive content in images, producing multimodal scams that evade text-based filters. Existing fraud detectors target pure-text short messages (SMS) and lack mechanisms for joint image–text reasoning. We propose GRPO-MMS, a reinforcement-learning framework based on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and driven by a composite reward for multimodal fraud detection. Three contributions are made. (i) We release MMS-VQA, a multimodal fraud dataset of 2,086 image–text pairs spanning eight categories and three input modalities (text-only, image-only, image–text), with a generator-based split for cross-domain evaluation. (ii) We design a three-component composite reward combining format, authenticity and scene rewards, where the scene reward injects fine-grained fraud-type gradients into GRPO advantage estimation. (iii) On Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 7B, GRPO yields up to +31.36 percentage points in 8-class accuracy and +21.39 pp in Macro-F1 on the image–text modality. Ablations show that a minimal scene-reward weight (λ = 0.05) is sufficient to activate fine-grained classification, achieving 81.50% 8-class accuracy.
